SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 1242
Date 8 / 9 / 34

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 7, 1934

QUEER TALE OF ARMS
FRAUD IN CHINA
Czecho-Slovak Citizen
On Trial After 10
Years' Lapse

PRAGUE, Aug. 12.—A 41-year-old Hungarian, M. Max Glass, a citizen of Czecho-Slovakia, is being tried at Chrudim, Bohemia, in connection with a remarkable arms fraud on the Chinese Government.
It is alleged that M. Glass, while in Shanghai in 1924, undertook to supply arms and ammunition to the Southern (Canton) Government and received about $12,000 advance payment.
When the boxes supposed to contain the goods were unpacked they were found to contain nothing but scrap iron.
The Chinese complained to the Czecho-Slovak authorities, but owing to administrative disorders in China ten years passed before the necessary documents reached Prague. Then a warrant was issued for M. Glass's arrest.
M. Glass denies the charge declaring that someone must have made unauthorized use of his personal papers when he was in China to practice the fraud in his name.—Reuter.

（批：See also B.649）

中国军火诈骗奇案
捷克斯洛伐克公民
在时隔十年后受审

布拉格，8月12日电。—一名41岁的匈牙利人、捷克斯洛伐克公民M. Max Glass（马克斯·格拉斯），因涉及一起针对中国政府的离奇军火诈骗案，正在波希米亚的赫鲁迪姆（Chrudim）接受审判。
据称，Glass先生于1924年在上海期间，承诺向南方（广州）政府供应军火和弹药，并收取了约12,000美元的预付款。
当那些据称装有货物的箱子被打开时，发现里面除了废铁外空无一物。
中方曾向捷克斯洛伐克当局提出抗议，但由于中国行政混乱，十年之后必要文件才送达布拉格。随后签发了逮捕Glass先生的令状。
Glass先生否认该项指控，声称有人在他身处中国期间未经授权使用了他的个人证件，以他的名义实施诈骗。—路透社。

（批注：另见 B.649）

THE SHANGHAI SPECTATOR

HOW THE SHANGHAI SPECTATOR
BLACKMAILED THE ASIA REALTY COMPANY
Read about it in our
next week's issue.

The Shanghai Spectator has never proceeded by hypocritical innuendos. The
Shanghai Spectator has never resorted to the practice of indicating people in order to be
protected from recourse by not mentioning by full name those it was driving at. And
furthermore dealing mainly with parties who know the English language this paper has
been incorporated under American law in order to give every one a fair chance to get at us
on their own grounds. And so, the Asia Realty Company now has the choice of two
jurisdictions.

AND WE INVITE THE ASIA REALTY TO SUE! AND ALL THE
THREATS, INTIMIDATION, AND OTHER METHODS THAT MIGHT BE CHOSEN
AGAINST US NOW OR IN THE FUTURE, WILL NOT STOP US FROM HAVING
OUR SAY-SO WHEN WE HAVE THE FACTS, WHEN WE ARE CONVINCED
OF THE FAIRNESS OF OUR CRITICISM EVEN SHOULD THE SPECTATOR
HAVE TO BE PUBLISHED ON A MIMEOGRAPH MACHINE. IT IS IMPORTANT
THAT THE PUBLIC SHOULD BE REMINDED HERE THAT WE HAVE ASKED
THE ASIA REALTY COMPANY BEFORE WE WROTE OUR ARTICLE LAST
WEEK TO EXPLAIN TO US HOW IT HAS PRODUCED THE ITEM OF
$1,366,895.61 THAT FIGURES ON THE CREDIT SIDE OF ITS WORKING ACCOUNT
WITHOUT A PLAUSIBLE EXPLANATION BEING AVAILABLE FOR THIS
AMOUNT.

It is important for the public to know that the Asia Realty Company has not been
able to answer nor has it, after our article appeared, used of its profuse means of publicity
in order to make its answer known to the anxious investors.

It is important for the public to know that when Mrs. Bowen of the Comacrib
Press requested us not to republish the Asia Realty article we suggested that the company
should either explain this item or undertake not to sell any more chits to the public until
its house had been cleaned. It must be interesting for the public to further note that Mrs.
Bowen accepted this as a useful and constructive suggestion and was hopeful in acting as
an intermediary to bring this understanding about. . . .

But alas, the Asia Realty could not see it that way. For cause. Alas.

Many statements entirely irrelevant to the subject matter have been made in defense of the Asia Realty Company's standing. The public will not be blinded by an artful sideshow or diversion.

But what the investing public is interested in at the present time are not spiritual discourses but facts simple plain down to earth facts. The public wants to know how about this $1,366,895.61 ?

The public also wants to know whether it is not true that the International Savings Society having had an investment of Tls. 1,200,000.00 in the Asia Realty Company, the I.S.S demanded early this year that these chits be reimbursed because the International Savings Society preferred to have its cash to the Asia Realty Debentures. And the public is also interested in knowing whether it is not true that, in order to avoid legal complications, the Asia Realty Company did comply with the wish of the I.S.S. and not having any cash at its disposal bartered properties against these chits. Is it not true also that early this year the Asia Realty whose income in our last week's article has been shown to be as low as 3.5 per cent (always provided that we accept the company's high valuation of its properties) went out in the open market, pressed for money, and borrowed over 1,000,000.00 at the exorbitant rate of 11% per year putting up as security some of its choicest lots?

It is regrettable that due to the disturbance caused to us by the triple switch of printers we have not had time to prepare our second instalment of the Asia Realty analysis. This however, we will do in time to be published in our next issue. In this new financial department of the Spectator we will at no time hasten to rush into print and so by chance make statements which have not had the full benefit of reflection and check For those who were unable to secure last week's issue we have available on the streets today this week's issue with last week's main article inserted at the exceptional price of 0.40 for the Special Edition while the regular edition can be procured as usual at 0.20 per copy.

为辩护亚西亚地产公司的地位，人们发表了许多与主题完全无关的声明。公众不会被巧妙的旁支插曲或转移视线的伎俩所蒙蔽。

但目前投资公众感兴趣的不是精神说教，而是简单、 plain、接地气的事实。公众想知道这1,366,895.61美元是怎么回事？

公众还想知道以下情况是否属实：国际储蓄会（International Savings Society）在亚西亚地产公司拥有1,200,000.00两白银的投资，该会今年早些时候要求偿还这些借据，因为国际储蓄会宁愿持有现金而非亚西亚地产公司的债券。公众也有兴趣知道，为了避免法律纠纷，亚西亚地产公司是否确实顺应了国际储蓄会的意愿，并在手头没有现金的情况下，用房产抵换这些借据。同样属实的是，今年早些时候，正如我们上周文章中所示，亚西亚地产公司的收入低至3.5%（前提是我们接受该公司对其房产的高估值），它走向公开市场，因资金紧缺，以每年11%的高昂利率借款超过1,000,000.00美元，并将其一些最优质的地块作为抵押？

遗憾的是，由于印刷商三次更换给我们造成的干扰，我们未能及时准备关于亚西亚地产公司分析的第二部分。不过，我们将及时完成并在下一期刊登。在《观察家报》这个新的财经栏目中，我们绝不会仓促付印，从而偶然发表未经充分思考和核查的声明。对于未能买到上周刊物的读者，我们今天在街头有售本周刊物，其中插入了上周的主要文章，特刊特价0.40元，而常规版仍可照常以每份0.20元购买。

关于亚西亚地产公司的更多重要事实。

Subject (in full) Ernst Borchers

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Ross

With reference to the letter of December 3, from the
Netherlands Consulate-General on the subject of Ernst Borchers,
this individual is a German, who speaks fluent Spanish, first
came to the notice of the Shanghai Municipal Police shortly
after arrival here in February, 1930. At this time he was
living in the Hotel Plaza. At first it was stated that
Borchers was connected with the firm Henry Krippendorf of Tientsin,
who acts as agents for Feng Yu Hsiang, but it later transpired
that he is the export manager of Spanish Firearms Manufacturing
Coy., Unceta and Company, Guernica, Spain. Nothing is known
locally against this concern which is reported to hold contracts
from the Spanish, Colombia, Ecuador and San Salvador Governments
for the supply of ASTRA automatic pistols and revolvers.
Shortly after arrival, Borchers through the medium of two
suspected arms dealers named Bisbjerg
Ax and Krausz, entered into
negotiations with a certain Li, a representative of Yen Shih Shan,
for the sale of a consignment of Astra rifle pistols with a
magazine capacity of 20 rounds each. The transaction called
for a deposit of $20,000. which was to be paid at the conclusion
of the provisional agreement concerning the arms which were to
be delivered to the Tsehow(澤州 )Arsenal, Shansi, by Borchers
personally. However, for some unknown reasons, the
negotiations fell through but were later renewed through the
mediation of a well known Russian Jew named A. G. Pisarevsky,
who was formerly in the employ of "Siemssen & Co." 218 Kiangsi
Road, where he acquired good connections with Chinese arms
dealers who are said to trust him. Pisarevsky is at present
working with Messrs. Marden & Company. It appears that
Pisarevsky was also unable to bring about a satisfactory agreement

he remained until June 9, and when he left he gave his destination
as Nanking.      In this connection it is interesting to note
that Borchers registered at the Pension Leineman, No. 6 Medhurst

On December 16, Borchers left Shanghai for Trieste

While in Shanghai Borchers appeared to make no

August, 1930, maintained that his business was perfectly

400,000 rounds of 7.63 ammunition. The consignment he said
had been shipped from Antwerp and that it was covered by "Huchoo".
During the course of this interview he strongly denied ever
having supplied arms to any Northern clique.
In view of the foregoing and in spite of Borchers'
claim that his business is perfectly legitimate, it would appear
that he is an individual whose activities would bear watching.

12月16日，博尔歇尔斯（Borchers）乘坐劳埃德·特里埃斯蒂诺轮船公司（Lloyd Triestine）的“VERITA”号轮船离开上海前往的里雅斯特（Trieste）。
在上海期间，博尔歇尔斯似乎并未试图隐瞒其业务性质，并在1930年8月与某位公职人员的谈话过程中，坚称其业务完全合法，并称他当时已与南京国民政府达成一笔交易，供应400支阿斯特拉（Astra）自动手枪，包括200支20发装和200支10发装，以及40万发7.63毫米弹药。他说这批货物已从安特卫普（Antwerp）装运，并持有“护照”（Huchoo）。
在这次面谈过程中，他强烈否认曾向任何北方派系提供武器。
鉴于上述情况，尽管博尔歇尔斯声称其业务完全合法，但他似乎是一个其活动值得监视的人。

SHANGHAI, 3rd December 1931.

Sir,

I have the honour to state that this morning Mr. Ernst
Borchers a German subject, born at Magdeburg on November 7th
1898 and holder of passport No. 1107, issued by the German
Consulate at Bilbao, Spain, on December 10th 1929, applied to
this Consulate General for a visa to the Netherlands East Indies.
He intends to leave in about a fortnight's time on a combined
business and pleasure trip.

Mr. Borchers states to be connected with a German-Spanish
factory of fire-arms at Guernica (Spain), represented in Shanghai
by Messrs. Astra China Co., 6 Szechuen Road, with which concern
he has been working during the last 9 months. His trip to Java
is also for the purpose of getting into touch with firms there,
who may be interested on the importation of his firm's manu-
factures. As his private address he mention the Pension
Leinemann, 6 Medhurst Road.

I should feel greatly obliged to learn whether the Municipal
Police is in possession of any information regarding this gen-
tleman.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

Chinese Secretary.

R.C.Aiers, Esquire,
Deputy Commissioner of Police,
Crime & Special Branches,
SHANGHAI.

博尔歇尔斯先生称其与位于西班牙格尔尼卡（Guernica）的一家德西合资枪械厂有关联，该厂在上海由四川路6号的阿斯特拉中国公司（Astra China Co.）代理，他在过去9个月里一直与该公司合作。他前往爪哇的目的也是为了与当地可能对其公司产品进口感兴趣的公司建立联系。他的私人住址列为麦赫斯特路（Medhurst Road）6号的莱内曼公寓（Pension Leinemann）。

Sir,

Mr. W. A. Skuse, Chief Tidesurveyor of the Chinese
Maritime Customs, is supervisor of the outdoor staff, conse-
quently is always in direct communication re the importing
of arms and ammunition to Shanghai, and also releasing of
same. He personally deals with all Huchaos for the land-
ing of explosives here, therefore, is in the position to en-
lighten us on enquiries referring to above particular goods,
and also to be on the outlook for same on information we may
obtain and extend to him. Since enquiries have commenced
on the importation of arms and ammunition to Shanghai he has
been interviewed by Chief Det. Insp. J. Hunter or the under-
signed. Also he receives the Huchaos for the importation
of explosives for the Nationalists Government, and deals with
the "Permit to land" and clearance of same. Huchaos of this
particular nature before landing and clearing are mostly veri-
fied, although signed by T. V. Soong or his secretary, by long
distant telephone calls to the Nationalists Government, Nan-
king. All necessary precautions are taken in the importations
of explosives for the government.

I am, Sir,

At 9.55 a.m. 28-7-30 the undersigned proceeded to the Spanish Consulate intending to interview the Consul General, but no interview took place because the Consul General was absent from Shanghai.

Subject (in full) Mayfair Bridge Club.
Made by D.P.S. Moore. Forwarded by W. Duncan, A.S.P.
Sir,
The above concern occupies two small rooms Nos.
104, 105 on the first floor at No. 151A Bubbling Well
Road. These two rooms were furnished and opened a short
while ago by Mrs. A.M. Moran residing at No. 607 Kiachow
Road, partly as a business venture and partly for the
sake of the game itself. As a business venture it has
failed hopelessly for although the place was introduced
to the public via the advertisement columns of the leading
foreign newspapers, it has no membership. The club is
controlled entirely by the owner and the few persons who
occasionally attend to play "bridge" are not allowed
credit, everything being conducted on a cash basis.
The lady in question is a widow about 45/50
years of age of independent means and a registered
British subject. She arrived in Shanghai in February
1930 from Sydney, Australia.
From observations made by the undersigned it
appears that the intention is to conduct the place as
a bona-fide club.

dancers. One of the latest
radio-singing machines sup-

is difficult to distinguish the
music dispensed from a full
orchestra. Dainty waitresses are
very attentive to one's wants,
and the whole shows a de-
sire to please and entertain.

Information has been received that E. Borchers, whose
business card is attached herewith, is a German, engaged in
arms dealing. He speaks Spanish fluently. He arrived in
Shanghai about the end of February 1930 and resided in the
Plaza Hotel, Room 301.
At first, it was stated that he was connected with the
firm Henry Krippendorf of Tientsin, who act as agents for
General Feng Yu-hsiang and whose local agent- Mr. Engstrom-
an American, resides at 39 Wonglo Road.
It later transpired that Borchers is the export manager
of the Spanish Firearms Manufacturing Company, Unceta & Co.,
Guernica, Spain.
Borchers entered into negotiations with a certain General
Li, a representative of General Yen Shi-shan, for the sale of
a consignment of an entirely new pattern of Mauser type rifle
the magazine of which contains 20 rounds. The intermediate
in this deal was Messrs Keeble & Co., which firm until recently
had an office at No. 46A Peking Road, but later removed to
No. 616 Avenue Road. The deal called for a deposit of $20,000
which General Li was to pay at the determination of the prelimi-
nary agreement for the supply of the arms to the Arsenal at
Tehchow, at which place Borchers was to deliver the goods
personally.
Borchers was introduced to General Li by Messrs Bjisberg
and the well known Krausz, which latter was sent to Shanghai
from Tientsin by Krippendorf. Bjisberg, who resided at 151c
Bubbling Well Road during these negotiations, was formerly
connected with well known arms firm, Heinzel, Ott & Co.,
who had offices at Tientsin and Shanghai. Ott is at present

起初，据说他与天津的 Henry Krippendorf 公司有联系，该公司充当冯玉祥将军的代理人，其本地代理人——美国人 Engstrom 先生——居住在翁洛路 (Wonglo Road) 39 号。
后来 выяснилось (原文为英语语境，此处意为“查明”) Borchers 是西班牙枪械制造公司 Unceta & Co.（位于西班牙格尔尼卡）的出口经理。
Borchers 与某位李将军（阎锡山将军的代表）进行了谈判，出售一批全新型号的毛瑟式步枪，其弹匣可容纳 20 发子弹。这笔交易的中间人是 Keeble & Co. 公司，该公司最近将办公室从北京路 (Peking Road) 46A 号迁至爱文义路 (Avenue Road) 616 号。交易要求支付 20,000 美元定金，李将军将在供应武器给德州兵工厂的初步协议确定时支付该定金，Borchers 将亲自在那裡交付货物。
Borchers 是由 Bjisberg 先生和著名的 Krausz 介绍给李将军的，后者是由 Krippendorf 从天津派往上海的。Bjisberg 在这些谈判期间居住在静安寺路 (Bubbling Well Road) 151c 号，他以前与著名的军火公司 Heinzel, Ott & Co. 有联系，该公司在天津和上海设有办事处。Ott 目前

Sir,
On or about November 15th 1924 the Czechoslovak
citizen Maxim GLAS entered into negotiations with
representatives of Marshall Chi regarding the sale of
arms and ammunition. It was arranged that the Chinese
officers should pay to him M. $ 80,000 on a deal worth
$ 165,000. Delivery should have been made within three
days. As security for the proper execution of the contract
on his behalf Glas handed over to the Chinese a number of
godown orders for sundry goods which were at that time
in his possession as representative of various German
firms. Having received the bargain money GLAS absconded.
No proceedings were taken by the Chinese, one reason being
that Marshall Chi was defeated at that time. Naturally, the
Chinese took possession of the sundry goods, which were
worth about $ 12,000.

Investigations by one of the German firms,
Messrs. Borchers & Firnhaber of Hamburg, revealed the
address of GLAS who is now residing in Germany.

The same firm now instructs me to make further
investigations in Shanghai, in order to enable them to
bring a charge of embezzlement against GLAS in the German
Courts.

I hereby beg to request you for copies of such reports
